title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building a combinatorial-topological description of the 'structure at infinity' of the moduli spaces M_{g,nu}, i.e. the boundary of the Deligne–Mumford compactification. On the previous pages he passes from the special case of a normal-crossings divisor on an analytic space to a general 'global stratification' of a space X into locally closed strata X_i. There he has spaces D*_{Delta_0} and D*_d.

This page (§88) defines a 'diagram of length nu' of a global stratification. It is a chain of closures of strata, Sigma_* = {X̄_{i0} ⊂ X̄_{i1} ⊂ ... ⊂ X̄_{inu}} (299). It is called non-degenerate (strict) when all inclusions are strict.

A strict local diagram is a pair (x, Sigma_*) with an 'origin' x. He requires x ∈ X_{i0} itself, not merely x in its closure X̄_{i0} (300).

He topologizes the set of strict local diagrams of length nu. A basic open set is obtained by fixing Sigma_* and letting x run through an open subset of the smallest stratum X_{i0}. The resulting space D*_{Delta_nu} is the disjoint union, over strict chains of length nu, of copies of the stratum X_{i0}. The map (x, Sigma_*) ↦ x (301, next page) is a local immersion, and the images of its connected components are strata.

On the next page he observes two things.
- The construction should really use the local stratification, i.e. chains of germs of strata at x, rather than global strata. Otherwise a self-intersecting divisor component is not 'unfolded'.
- In the normal-crossings case one should recover the coverings D*_{Delta_r} = ⊔ D*_{d_r} of the previous sections. These are essentially the normalizations of the depth-r strata decorated by flags of local branches.

The declared next goal is to define the analogue of the 'specialization morphisms' between these diagram spaces. These are face/degeneracy-type maps between chain lengths, together with the gluing (tubular-neighbourhood / tangential base point) data needed to compare fundamental groupoids at different depths.

In effect he is building a simplicial-type object over the nerve of the poset of strata: in degree nu, the space of flags of strata of length nu pointed at the deepest stratum. This is meant to serve as a combinatorial model of the stratified space at infinity.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. Note that with global strata the map D*_{Delta_nu} -> X is injective on each piece and is really a disjoint union of strata. The 'covering' phenomenon of the normal-crossings case (several local branches through a point) only appears with the germ-of-strata version Grothendieck mentions on the next page. As defined here, the global version does not recover the D*_d coverings when divisor components self-intersect. Grothendieck himself flags this.
The phrase 'x variable dans un ouvert de Sigma_*' should be read as an open subset of X_{i0}, which is what the definition requires.

ideas.what: Space of strict chains (flags) of strata of a stratified space, pointed at a point of the deepest stratum, with a topology making it a local immersion to X
ideas.modern_name: Nerve of the poset of strata / space of flags of strata. Close to the 'exit-path' or 'link' simplicial structures of a stratified space, and to the normalized boundary strata with branch flags for a normal-crossings divisor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Exit-path categories: MacPherson (unpublished), Treumann 2009, Lurie (Higher Algebra, appendix). Simplicial description of normal-crossings boundaries: Deligne (Hodge II, 1971), dual complexes
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) announces a theory of tame ('modérée') stratified spaces and the structure at infinity of M_{g,nu}, but not this explicit construction

ideas.what: Insistence that the origin lie in the open stratum X_{i0}, not its closure, and the remark that one should use germs of strata (local stratification) rather than global strata
ideas.modern_name: Distinction between a stratification and its locally unibranch / normalized version; local branch data at normal-crossings points
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Deligne's mixed Hodge theory, normal-crossings combinatorics)

ideas.what: Planned 'specialization morphisms' between diagram spaces of different lengths
ideas.modern_name: Specialization / cospecialization maps along strata; tangential base points; gluing data of the boundary of DM compactifications in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Ihara, Nakamura; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (Teichmüller tower)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a general, stratification-theoretic (not only normal-crossings) simplicial space of pointed strata-flags. He intends to equip it with specialization morphisms to model the structure at infinity, an early outline of an exit-path-type combinatorial model for stratified spaces. The development (germ-of-strata version, specialization maps) is left unfinished.
missed.quote: On appelle diagramme de longueur ν∈ℕ d'une stratification globale tout système Σ_* = {X̄_{i0} ⊂ X̄_{i1} … ⊂ X̄_{iν}} de strates
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly of historical interest. It documents Grothendieck's pre-Esquisse route toward tame stratified topology for M_{g,nu}, which parallels the later exit-path / stratified homotopy theory. The mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but routine definition of the space of pointed flags of strata. Historically it shows Grothendieck generalizing the normal-crossings boundary combinatorics of M̄_{g,nu} to arbitrary stratifications, in line with the Esquisse program. There is no finished result beyond what is standard today.
transcription_corrections: 'le diagramme est un diagramme [?] si les inclusions sont strictes' should read roughly 'le diagramme est non dégénéré si les inclusions sont strictes' (underlined word, likely 'non dégénéré').
The insertion above 'sur l'ensemble des diagrammes' appears to be 'locaux stricts', not '(avec strates)'.
'x variable dans un ouvert de Σ_*' is likely 'x variable dans un ouvert de X_{i0}' (written 'de Σ_x' or similar).
Crossed out after 'origine': '[-x∈X_{i0}-] ... NB'. The marginal NB reads 'NB on exige x ∈ X_{i0} et non seulement x ∈ X̄_{i0}'.
The page number at top is 88, with a crossed-out number beside it.
